quote: The sabbath was given to the Jews to be observed literally, like other things, as rites symbolically signifying something deeper. A particular kind of vacation, you see, was enjoined on them. Take care to carry out what that vacation signifies. A spiritual vacation, I mean, is tranquility of heart; but tranquility of heart issues from the serenity of a good conscience. So the person who really observes the sabbath is the one who doesn't sin. This, after all, is the way the command was given to those who were commanded to observe the sabbath: "You shall perform no servile work." "Everyone who commits sin is the slave of sin."

Two loaves of bread made from the first fruits of the new harvest were rightly ordered to be offered, for the church gathers those it can consecrate to its Redeemer as a new family from both peoples, the Jews and the Gentiles.

He who is "perfect" is taught by God himself concerning the meaning of the festivals, and he does not need a man as his teacher for learning these things, but he learns from God, if anyone is able to grasp the voice of God. But he who is not such a one, but of lower rank, learns from him who has learned from God. There is, then, this twofold manner of teaching concerning the festivals. There is the one by which the prophetic mind, illumined through the Spirit, is taught — which, so to speak, is learned more by the gaze of the mind than by the sound of a voice, through which the truth itself, and not the shadow and image of the truth, is recognized.
